sections.title: Thinning and sprinkling: from robust sampling to almost Hamiltonicity
sections.abstract: The authors develop a thinning–sprinkling method for robustness under random vertex sampling and use it to obtain almost-Hamilton cycles in several highly connected graph families.
sections.claimed_result: The framework gives asymptotic solutions to cited Chvátal and Lovász Hamiltonicity conjectures under polylogarithmic hypotheses.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Tough, connected vertex-transitive, nearly regular expander, and k-connected graphs with k=ω(log n), as applicable.
sections.caveat: New preprint; proof not independently checked.

sections.title: Bounded-orbit wandering domains do not exist
sections.abstract: The paper rules out bounded-forward-orbit wandering Fatou components for transcendental entire functions and proves a stronger meromorphic statement.
sections.claimed_result: Every point in a wandering domain of a transcendental meromorphic function has unbounded orbit, according to the authors.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Transcendental entire or meromorphic dynamics and wandering domains.
sections.caveat: Long-standing-question resolution is a preprint claim requiring expert verification.

sections.title: Global well-posedness and scattering for the three-dimensional focusing energy-critical NLS
sections.abstract: The authors claim global well-posedness and scattering below both ground-state energy and gradient thresholds for focusing energy-critical NLS in R^3.
sections.claimed_result: The abstract says this confirms the three-dimensional threshold conjecture.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Focusing energy-critical NLS on R^3 below the stated thresholds.
sections.caveat: First-day preprint; interaction Morawetz and concentration-compactness arguments not checked.

sections.title: Stable solutions of the Allen–Cahn equation in dimension three are one-dimensional
sections.abstract: Every bounded stable Allen–Cahn solution in R^3 is claimed to be one-dimensional, with a consequence for De Giorgi's conjecture in dimension four.
sections.claimed_result: The authors state the three-dimensional classification and the dimension-four monotone consequence.
sections.caveat: The abstract does not specify all proof hypotheses.

sections.title: A 1/64 spectral gap for surfaces with δ=1/2
sections.abstract: The authors prove an essential spectral gap for convex co-compact hyperbolic surfaces, obtaining 1/64−ε at δ=1/2.
sections.claimed_result: A new Fractal Uncertainty Principle yields the stated quantitative gap.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Convex co-compact hyperbolic surfaces with δ in (2/5,14/27).

sections.title: A Peterson program for general Schubert varieties and mirror symmetry
sections.abstract: The paper extends Peterson-variety and mirror-symmetry constructions to arbitrary Schubert varieties and formulates quantum-cohomology conjectures.
sections.claimed_result: Generalized Peterson varieties and superpotentials are constructed; key identifications are conjectured and some type-A divisor cases verified.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Schubert varieties, flag varieties, Langlands duality, smooth Fano cases.
sections.caveat: Central general quantum-cohomology statements are conjectural.

sections.title: Frobenius lifts and point counting for smooth curves
sections.abstract: An algorithm computes zeta functions of smooth curves over finite fields through lifted Frobenius and de Rham cohomology.
sections.claimed_result: The method has softly cubic field-degree complexity for general smooth planar curves and improves a crystalline-Frobenius preservation statement under ramification at most p.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Proper smooth finite-field curves with a lift to a p-adic valuation ring.
sections.caveat: Practical complexity and implementation remain unassessed.

sections.title: Diophantine approximation by primes and Landau–Siegel zeros
sections.abstract: Conditional on Siegel-zero hypotheses, the authors obtain infinitely many primes giving strong Diophantine approximations to αp+β.
sections.claimed_result: The paper gives p^(−1/3+ε) and stronger p^(−1/3−1/20) approximation bounds under two conditional hypotheses.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Irrational α of finite type, real β, small ε, and the stated Siegel-zero assumptions.
sections.caveat: The results are conditional and do not establish Siegel zeros.
